title: Zapier alternatives, with checked prices | 50agents
description: Zapier alternatives: Make and n8n for cheaper multi-step runs, Power Automate for Microsoft 365, 50agents to build from plain words. Prices checked.
answer: If Zapier costs too much because every step counts as a task, Make bills by credit from $9 a month and n8n bills once per run, however many steps it has.
If you live in Microsoft 365, Power Automate may already be in your licence; if you would rather describe the job than wire up steps, 50agents builds it from plain words.
ask: Set up an automation: every new HubSpot contact is added as a row to my Google Sheet and posted in a Slack channel
lede: Most people leave over the bill: Zapier counts every action step as a task, code and AI steps included.

entries.suits: Small teams who know what they want done but not how to wire it. Captain picks the kind, asks what it cannot know, and shows the plan before it builds.
entries.limit: It connects 2,300+ apps, not Zapier's 10,541+, and there is no drag-and-drop editor: you change steps by asking in chat.

entries.suits: People who think in diagrams. Every scenario sits on a canvas, so branches, filters and loops are visible, and it bills by credit rather than by task.
entries.price: Free: 1,000 credits a month. Core: from $9 a month (10,000 credits)
entries.limit: Most actions still cost a credit each, so a long scenario is not cheap just because the canvas makes it easy to build.

entries.suits: Teams with someone technical. One execution is one run of the whole workflow, however many steps, and a code node takes over when the built-in steps run out.
entries.price: No free cloud plan. Starter: €20 a month billed yearly (2.5K executions)
entries.limit: There is no free cloud plan, prices are in euros and billed yearly, and the cheapest plan stops at 2.5K executions a month.

entries.suits: Companies on Microsoft 365 who mostly connect Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and Excel. A free licence for work accounts covers cloud flows with standard connectors.
entries.price: Free for cloud flows with standard connectors. Premium: $15.00 per user a month, paid yearly
entries.limit: Premium connectors, which cover many non-Microsoft apps, need a Premium licence at $15 per user, or a Process licence.

entries.suits: Teams who want Zapier's simplicity without per-task billing: open source, free for up to 5 users, and the option to host it yourself.
entries.price: Free: 1,000 credits, up to 5 users. Plus: $20 a month flat (10,000 credits)
entries.limit: It lists 770+ apps, so check yours are there before you move anything.

entries.suits: People whose Zaps were really about email and meetings: triaging the inbox, drafting replies, booking calls. Lindy is an AI assistant first, and asks before acting outside.
entries.price: $50 in credits for 7 days. Team: from $29.99 a month per active user
entries.limit: Every active user is billed, and credit-using actions pause when the pool runs low.

us: You can say what you want in plain words but have never built a Zap, or the person who needs it is not the person who builds them.
The job needs judgement on each run (an AI agent), a website with no app (a browser agent) or records of its own (an app).
You want every message to a customer to wait for your yes by default.
them: You rely on an app only Zapier connects. With 10,541+ apps it covers the long tail better than anyone.
Your Zaps are short and well under your task limit. Moving them saves little and costs a weekend.
You are a larger company that needs SCIM and role-based access today.

move.title: List what runs
move.body: Open your Zaps list, sort by last run and write down only the Zaps that ran this month, with their trigger app and each step. Old Zaps rarely need moving.

move.title: Export if your plan allows it
move.body: Team and Enterprise accounts can export Zaps as JSON. Free and Professional cannot, so screenshot each Zap's steps instead. Neither imports elsewhere; it is your checklist.

move.title: Rebuild the busiest one first
move.body: Start with the Zap that uses the most tasks: that is where the savings are. Describe it to Captain in plain words and check the plan it shows against your notes.

move.title: Run both for a week, then switch off
move.body: Leave the Zap on while the new one runs, compare the results each day, then turn the Zap off. Keep it off, not deleted, for a month.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest Zapier alternative?
faqs.a: For a few simple automations, Make has a free plan with 1,000 credits a month, and Activepieces is free for up to 5 users. For many long workflows, n8n is usually cheapest per run because it bills per execution, not per step.

faqs.q: Is there a free Zapier alternative?
faqs.a: Yes. Make gives 1,000 credits a month free, Activepieces gives 1,000 credits and up to 5 users, and 50agents is free to start. Zapier's own free plan is 100 tasks a month with two-step Zaps.

faqs.q: Which Zapier alternative has the most apps?
faqs.a: Make lists 3,500+ apps, n8n's directory lists 2,829 integrations and 50agents works with 2,300+ through viaSocket. None matches Zapier's 10,541+.

faqs.q: Can I import my Zaps into another tool?
faqs.a: Not directly. Zapier's JSON export, on Team and Enterprise, imports only into Zapier. Every alternative means rebuilding, so start with the Zaps that matter.
